stimulus.body: For this problem, a two-valued tree structure has 15 internal (non-leaf) nodes. Exactly how many external null end nodes does it have?

questions.stem: For this problem, a two-valued tree structure has 15 internal (non-leaf) nodes. Exactly how many external null end nodes does it have?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "assumes equal numbers of internal and external nodes" gives 15, not 16.
Wrong belief "doubles the internal count" gives 30, not 16.
Wrong belief "subtracts instead of adding one" gives 14, not 16.

questions.explanation: In any binary tree the number of external leaves exceeds the number of internal nodes by one, so 15 internal nodes give 16 external leaves.
questions.hint: External leaves are internal nodes plus one.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving binary trees and traversals.
questions.stem: In the given setup, a complete binary tree has height 5. What is the maximum number of nodes it can contain?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "counts only the deepest level" gives 32, not 63.
Wrong belief "omits the final subtraction of one" gives 64, not 63.
Wrong belief "adds one instead of subtracting" gives 65, not 63.

questions.explanation: A complete binary tree of height 5 has all levels filled, giving 2 to the power (5+1) minus 1 nodes, namely 63.
questions.hint: Sum the geometric series of level sizes.
